title: Prejudice, Stereotypes & Discrimination
summary: Prejudice (negative attitude), stereotypes (overgeneralised beliefs) and discrimination (unfair behaviour). Causes, consequences and reduction strategies.
revision: Prejudice, stereotypes and discrimination: definitions, causes and reduction strategies.
traps: Prejudice = attitude, stereotype = belief, discrimination = behaviour.
Contact hypothesis: cooperative, equal-status contact reduces prejudice.

notes.t: A negative attitude or feeling toward a group and its members, often without adequate basis.
An overgeneralised belief about a group, applying the same traits to all members.
Unfair or negative behaviour toward a group or its members.

i: Social learning: observing prejudiced attitudes in family and peers
Realistic conflict theory: competition over limited resources
Social identity: in-group favouritism and out-group derogation
Contact hypothesis: cooperative interaction under equal status
Superordinate goals: shared goals requiring cooperation

notes.t: UGC NET frequently asks to distinguish prejudice, stereotypes and discrimination, and to identify prejudice-reduction strategies.

mnemonics.title: PSD
mnemonics.text: P — Prejudice (negative attitude), S — Stereotype (overgeneralised belief), D — Discrimination (unfair behaviour)

flashcards.a: Cooperative interaction under equal status reduces prejudice.
